question.text: Rain drops fall vertically at a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m </mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. At what angle (in degree) do they fall on the wind screen of a car moving with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m </mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, if the wind screen is inclined at an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>23</mn><mo>°</mo></math> to the vertical? [<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mfenced><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>75</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>≈</mo><mn>37</mn><mo>°</mo></math>]

solution.text:
tan(90°-θ)=2015

∴cotθ=2015=43

⇒ θ=37°

∴ ϕ=37°+23°=60° (Angle made with the windscreen)
